readerTitle: The partner with 5,000 customers sold almost nothing
caseNote: 가상 사례 (산업용 씰 제조사와 두 파트너, 사내 데이터 도구 팀) · 모든 수치는 설명용
insight: 파트너가 채널이 되는 조건은 고객 수가 아니라, 내 제품을 파는 일이 파트너 자신의 목표를 움직이느냐이다.
misconception: 고객이 많은 큰 파트너와 계약하면 그 고객들에게 자동으로 팔린다.

sources.text: 유통·채널 관리의 일반 원리 (파트너 인센티브 정렬)
모든 사례와 수치는 설명용 가상 예시

factChecks.note: 유통사 고객 5,000곳, 6개월 주문 12건, 정비 업체 기술자 40명 등은 모두 설명용 가상 수치입니다. 실제 업계 통계처럼 읽히지 않도록 카드에 illustrative 라벨이 붙었는지 확인하세요.
MKT-06-05(중간상 마진), MKT-06-06(고객 소유)과 겹치지 않도록 마진 구조와 고객 관계 소유 문제는 Watch out 카드에서 한 줄로만 언급했습니다. 형제 레슨 최종본과 표현이 충돌하지 않는지 확인하세요.

cards.title: The partner with 5,000 customers sold almost nothing
body: A small factory makes a long-lasting seal for industrial pumps. It signs a deal with a big distributor that supplies 5,000 plants.
Six months later: 12 orders. Meanwhile, a tiny repair firm nobody paid attention to is ordering every week.

image.label: A giant warehouse shelf with one small box gathering dust
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 수천 개 상자가 꽉 찬 거대한 창고 선반 구석에 작은 상자 하나가 먼지를 뒤집어쓰고 있음. 옆에는 작은 정비 트럭이 같은 상자를 싣고 떠나는 모습. 실제 기업 로고와 상표는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Which partner would you sign first?
body: Your seal costs more than standard ones but lasts three times longer. It takes a minute to explain why.
You have time to support one partner well. Who do you pick?

options.text: A national distributor with 5,000 plant customers and 40,000 products in its catalog
options.feedback: Huge reach, and a listing costs you little. But your seal becomes one line among 40,000, sold by reps who move what's easy.

options.text: A regional repair firm whose 40 technicians get called back, unpaid, when a pump leaks again
options.feedback: Far smaller reach, but every seal they install cuts their own costly callbacks. They have a reason to push it.

options.text: A trade association that will email your brochure to its members
options.feedback: Cheap and wide. But an email nobody is rewarded for acting on rarely turns into orders.

cards.title: Reach was there. A reason to sell wasn't.
body: The distributor's reps are paid on total sales. A new seal that needs explaining earns them less per minute than reordering gaskets customers already know.
So the seal sat in the catalog. Nobody was against it. Nobody had a reason to bring it up.
The repair firm was different. Each leak that came back cost a free second visit. Their technicians started fitting the long-life seal on every job and telling plant managers why.

cards.title: Partners as channels
body: A **partner channel** is another business that already reaches your customers and passes your product along: a distributor, an installer, a consultant, a platform.
The partner's reach is only potential. It turns into sales when selling your product **moves the partner's own numbers**: more revenue, fewer problems, happier clients.

image.label: Two pipes to customers: a wide one blocked, a thin one flowing
image.brief: 인포그래픽. 왼쪽에 굵은 파이프("Big reach")가 중간에 밸브로 막혀 있고 밸브에 "What's in it for them?" 라벨. 오른쪽 얇은 파이프("Small reach")에서는 제품이 고객 쪽으로 계속 흘러감. 실제 로고 없음.

cards.title: Three questions before you sign.
body: A partner will actually sell for you when the answer to all three is yes:
list: **Does it help their goal?** Revenue, fewer complaints, a stronger offer to their clients
**Does it fit how they already work?** Same visits, same customers, same buying moment
**Is it easy to sell?** Can a busy rep explain it in one sentence?
cards.callout: A signed agreement answers none of these.
cards.softwareNote: Being listed in an app marketplace or an integration directory is the software version of a catalog line. It works when the partner's own users ask for it, or when the partner's team earns something by recommending it.

cards.title: Reach is who they could tell. Motivation is whether they will.
body: Founders compare partners by size because size is easy to count. Motivation is harder to see, so it gets skipped.

This doesn't mean big partners are bad. A large distributor with a real reason to sell you, such as a gap in its range that customers complain about, can be the best channel you'll ever have. The test is the same at any size.
Often the smaller, hungrier partner proves the case first, and that proof is what gets the big one interested.

cards.title: A motivated partner still needs your time.
body: Partners sell on their priorities, not yours. When their goals shift, your sales can drop without warning.
Even a willing partner needs training, sales material and quick answers from you. Spread that support across ten partners and none of them gets enough.
And every partner takes a cut and sits between you and the customer. Those costs are real, and the next lessons look at them.

cards.title: Now you're a team inside a big company.
body: Your internal data team built a tool that turns sales numbers into a weekly forecast in minutes. You want the company's 300 sales reps to use it. You can recruit one internal partner.
Who helps most?

options.text: The CEO, who will announce it at the next all-hands meeting
options.feedback: Huge reach and a strong signal. But after the meeting, nobody's own work changes, so use often fades within weeks.

options.text: Sales operations, who spend every Friday building the forecast by hand
options.feedback: Your tool gives them their Fridays back, so they'll ask reps to use it and fix problems for you. Smaller voice, real reason.

options.text: IT, who can install it on every rep's laptop by default
options.feedback: Everyone gets it, which looks like success. But installed isn't used, and IT gains nothing from reps opening it.

cards.title: A partner is a channel only when selling you helps them.
body: Judge partners by what your product does for their goals, not by how many customers they have.
**Try it today:** pick one current or possible partner. Write one sentence on how selling your product makes their week better. If you can't, fix that before you ask for more.
